(p-٥٨٧٤) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Mulk

Al-Mahayimi said: It was named so because it includes many of the things that dominion (al-mulk) should entail: abundance of goods, the all-encompassing power, giving life and causing death, testing the deeds of people, victory and forgiveness, raising buildings for its servants, equality among its subjects, adorning its lands, subduing its enemies, showing mercy to its friends, security and low prices, and that no one can help one who opposes Him or provide sustenance to one whom He withholds from. End of quote.

It is also called Surah Tabaraka. It is a Meccan surah, and its number of verses is thirty.

(p-٥٨٧٥) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying:

[1] ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent.﴾

﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That is, exalted is He in whose hand is the dominion of this world and the Hereafter and their authority; His command and decree are executed in both of them, and He, regarding whatever He wills to do, is possessed of power that no one can prevent, and no incapacity stands between Him and it.

Al-Qashani said: Dominion (al-mulk) is the world of bodies, just as the realm of the unseen (al-malakut) is the world of souls. Therefore He described His essence, with regard to His directing the world of dominion according to His will, with "tabaraka" (blessed), which is the utmost of greatness and the furthest extent of increase in exaltation and blessing; and with regard to His subjugating the world of the malakut, according to the requirement of His will, with "tasbih" (glorification), which is transcendence, as in His saying: ﴿So glorified is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things﴾ [Ya-Sin: 83], each used in what suits it; for greatness, increase and blessing suit bodies, and transcendence suits what is free of matter. So the meaning of "tabaraka" is that He, the Exalted, is great and magnificent, who disposes of the world of dominion by the hand of His power, and no one else disposes of it. So everything of bodies that exists is in His hand, not in the hand of another; He directs them as He wills, and He is the One capable of everything among possible things that does not exist, bringing them into existence as He wills.

The commentary on His saying, the Exalted:

[2] ﴿He who created death and life that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed; and He is the Almighty, the Forgiving.﴾

﴿He who created death and life that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾: i.e., He decreed death and life (p-5876). So He causes to die whom He wills and as He wills, and gives life to whom He wills and as He wills, until a known term. Or, He brought life into existence and removed it, according to what He had decreed.

Al-Qashani said: Death and life belong to the category of privation and possession (al-'adam wa al-malakah). Life is perception and voluntary movement, even if involuntary, like breathing. Death is the absence of that in what is by nature capable of having it. The absence of possession is not pure nonexistence; rather, there is in it a trace of existence. Pain requires a substrate that receives the existential attribute, which is why the act of creation may be related to it, just as it is related to life. The purpose of creating both is the trial of human beings regarding the goodness and badness of their deeds; that is, the knowledge that follows the known thing, upon which reward is based. This is the knowledge that appears in human manifestations after the known thing has occurred, for it is nothing but God's knowledge hidden in the unseen, which becomes manifest when the known thing becomes manifest. For life is that by which one is enabled to perform deeds, and death is what calls to and motivates the goodness of deeds, and through it the effects of deeds become apparent, just as through life its roots become apparent; and by them souls differ in ranks and vary in perdition and salvation. He mentioned death before life because death in the science of dominion (ʿilm al-mulk) is essential, while life is accidental. It was said: if by it is meant the prior nonexistence, its precedence is evident, since it precedes existence; or if the subsequent nonexistence is meant, its being mentioned first is because it contains admonition, reminder, and deterrence from committing sins.

﴿And He is the Almighty﴾: i.e., the Dominant who overpowers whoever does evil in deed. ﴿the Forgiving﴾: i.e., for the sins of whoever turns back to Him in repentance and does good in deed.

(p-٥٨٧٧) The Quranic verse:

﴿Who created seven heavens in layers. You see no imbalance in the creation of the Most Merciful. So return your gaze; do you see any fissure?﴾

﴿Who created seven heavens in layers﴾. Ibn Jarir said: "Tabaqan" means one layer above another, some of them above others.

Al-Mahayimi said: That is, they agree with one another without contradiction, so that the wisdom in what comes into being and what passes away may be completed.

Some astronomers ('ulama' al-falak) said: Know that the word "sama'" (heaven) is used linguistically for everything that is above a person, since it derives from "sumuww," which means height. Thus the roof of a house is a "sama'." From this is God's words: ﴿Let him extend a rope to the sky, then let him cut it off﴾ [al-Hajj: 15], meaning, let him extend a rope to the roof of his house. This boundless expanse is also a "sama'." From this is God's words: ﴿like a good tree whose root is firm and whose branches are in the sky﴾ [Ibrahim: 24]. Clouds are also a "sama'." From this is God's words: ﴿He sent down water from the sky﴾ [al-Ra'd: 17]. The celestial bodies are also "samawat" (heavens). Therefore, the seven heavens mentioned often in the Noble Quran are these seven wandering bodies (planets). They are "tibaq," meaning that some of them are above others, because the orbit (falak) of each of them is above the orbit of the others.

﴿You see no imbalance in the creation of the Most Merciful﴾: that is, no contradiction or lack of proportion in observing wisdom; rather, He has observed it in all His creation.

﴿So return your gaze﴾: that is, if you doubt, repeat the look. ﴿Do you see any fissure?﴾: that is, any flaw. The original meaning of "futur" is splits and cracks; it has been said that it is used here for what it entails, as they have said, but the correct view is that it is in its literal sense. That is: do you see any rupture or severance between the heavens, such that the connections of the celestial bodies are broken, separating them, cutting their ties and the cords of their mutual attraction? No! Rather, they are mutually attracted, each bound to the others on every side, as was mentioned earlier in Surah Qaf in the verse: ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, and it has no fissures?﴾ [Qaf: 6].

(p-٥٨٧٨)

**The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[4] ﴿Then return the gaze twice; the gaze will return to you humbled while it is weary.﴾

﴿Then return the gaze﴾ means: repeat it. ﴿Twice﴾ means: two more returns, seeking a flaw, a defect, or a fault. The dual here is used to mean repetition.

﴿Will return﴾ means: will come back. ﴿To you, the gaze, humbled﴾ means: repelled from reaching what it sought.

﴿While it is weary﴾ means: exhausted and worn out.

**Remarks:**

**First:** Al-Zamakhshari (ʿal-Zamakhsharī) held that His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿You see in the creation of the Most Merciful no disproportion﴾ [al-Mulk: 3], is a second attribute of His saying ﴿seven heavens﴾ [al-Mulk: 3]. He placed ﴿the creation of the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Mulk: 3] in the position of the pronoun, for magnification, while the original would be "in them." Al-Qadi (al-Bayḍāwī) and al-Qashani followed him. His wording is:

"It is the utmost perfection of the world of dominion, for they are the heavens. You will not see a creation more precise, or an order and layering more beautiful than them. He attributed their creation to the Most Merciful because they are among the roots of the manifest blessings and the origins of all the worldly blessings. He negated disproportion from them because some of them correspond to others, and because of the excellence of their arrangement and their harmony. He said, ﴿Then return the gaze twice﴾, because repeated looking and the roaming of thought establish the realities of things. When this is so regarding them while seeking breaches and cracks, it yields nothing but repulsion and exhaustion, and the impossibility is established. How wearied is the one who seeks the existence of the impossible." End of quotation.

If His saying ﴿You see in the creation of the Most Merciful no disproportion﴾ [al-Mulk: 3] were taken as a new, independent statement, affirmed in its generality for the harmony and perfection of His creation and the consummate beauty of it, so that it encompasses what precedes it, that would be better than restricting it to being a descriptive attribute of what precedes it. It would be like the verse ﴿who perfected everything He created﴾ [al-Sajdah: 7] and the verse ﴿the handiwork of Allah, who perfected all things﴾ [al-Naml: 88]. Some have refined this by saying: the verse contains an indication of a syllogism whose form is: "You do not see in it any disproportion, because it is of His creation, Exalted is He; and you do not see in His creation any disproportion."

**Second:** Imam Ibn Ḥazm, may Allah have mercy on him, has a discussion of this verse in his book *al-Fiṣal*, which he included in his debates with the Mu'tazilites. We quote it here for its vigour. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

"The disproportion that is familiar is that which is repugnant to souls or departs from what is customary. We call a distorted form to have disproportion. This, then, is not the disproportion which Allah, Exalted is He, negated from His creation. Therefore it is not what people call disproportion. Nothing remains except that the disproportion which Allah, Exalted is He, negated from what He created is something that does not exist in it at all. For if disproportion existed in the creation of Allah, Exalted is He, the saying of Allah, Exalted is He, ﴿You see in the creation of the Most Merciful no disproportion﴾ [al-Mulk: 3], would be refuted, and none refutes Allah, Exalted is He, except a disbeliever. Thus the assumption of the Mu'tazilites is invalidated, that disbelief, injustice, lying, and oppression are disproportion, for all of that exists in the creation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is seen in it, and is witnessed by sight in it. Thus their argument is invalidated.

"If someone says: what then is this disproportion which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed that it is not seen in His creation?

"It is said to them: it is a name that applies to no existing referent in the world at all, but is wholly non-existent. For if it were something existing in the world, disproportion would be found in the creation of Allah, Exalted is He. Allah, Exalted is He, has denied this and informed that it is not seen in His creation.

"Then we say, and success is from Allah, Exalted is He: The whole world other than Allah, Exalted is He, is entirely created by Allah, Exalted is He, its bodies and its accidents all of them, we except nothing from them. Then when the observer considers the division of the kinds of its accidents and the kinds of its bodies, the division proceeds evenly in the preference of its genera and species, by their defining limits that distinguish them and their differentiae that separate them, on one level and one configuration, down to the individuals that come under the species of species. There is no disproportion in any of that whatsoever, in any respect, and no divergence in any of it at all. Whoever understands this knows that the form we deem ugly falls together under the category of shape and outline, then under the category of quality, then under the name of accident, falling evenly with no superiority in it, and no disproportion in this respect of the division.

"Likewise we know that disbelief and belief in the heart both fall under the category of conviction, then under the act of the soul, then under quality and accident, falling evenly with no superiority in it, and no disproportion from this aspect of the division. Likewise we know that belief and disbelief by the tongue both fall under the category of an air-branch by means of the instruments of speech, then under the category of motion, then under the category of quality, and under the name of accident, falling truly and evenly with no disproportion or difference in it.

"The same applies to injustice and equity, to justice and oppression, to truthfulness and lying, and to fornication and lawful intercourse. Likewise is everything in the world, until all existing things return to the first primary categories above which there is no higher category that unites them, except that they are created by Allah, Exalted is He: these are substance, quantity, quality, and relation. Thus disproportion is negated from everything Allah, Exalted is He, has created, and the aforementioned verse returns as a proof against the Mu'tazilites, by a necessity from which they have no escape: namely, that if the existence of disbelief, lying, and injustice were disproportion, as they claim, then disproportion would exist in the creation of the Most Merciful, and Allah, Exalted is He, has refuted that, namely that disproportion should be seen in His creation." End of his words.

**Third:** Al-Nāṣir (Ibn al-Munīr) said: In His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿the gaze will return to you humbled﴾, there is the placing of the apparent noun in the position of the pronoun. Its benefit includes an alert that what returns humbled and exhausted does not perceive the flaws, and that is the instrument by which one seeks to perceive what exists. When nothing is perceived, this indicates that there is nothing.

[5]

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven with lamps, and made them missiles against the devils, and prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.﴾

﴿And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven with lamps.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: They are the stars. He made them "lamps" because of their light. Likewise, the morning (subh) is only called subh because of the light that shines for people from the day.

﴿And We made them missiles against the devils.﴾ Ibn Kathir said: The pronoun in His words, Exalted is He, (p-5881) ﴿and made them﴾ refers to the category of lamps, not to the stars themselves, because the stars that are in the sky are not what is hurled at; rather, it is flaming meteors (shuhub) from beyond them, though they may be drawn from them. And God knows best.

The judge (al-Qadi) said: That is, We made for them (the stars) another benefit, namely the stoning of your enemies by the shooting down of the meteors caused by them. It has also been said: The meaning is: We made them missiles and conjectures against the devils of mankind, namely the astrologers.

Al-Shihab said: He (al-Qadi) deemed this weak, because it contradicts the apparent meaning as transmitted (al-ma'thur). The word "rajm" can be used in the sense of conjecture (zann), as a known figurative usage (majaz, a non-literal use of a word). The verse has the same meaning as the verse of al-Saffat: ﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with the adornment of the stars﴾ [al-Saffat: 6] ﴿and as protection from every rebellious devil﴾ [al-Saffat: 7] ﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly, and they are pelted from every side﴾ [al-Saffat: 8] ﴿repelled, and for them is a enduring punishment﴾ [al-Saffat: 9] ﴿except one who snatches a fragment, so there follows him a piercing flame﴾ [al-Saffat: 10] ﴿And We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze﴾, that is, in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 67, verse 6–11:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[6–11] ﴿And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾ ﴿When they are thrown into it, they will hear from it a roaring as it boils up.﴾ [Al-Mulk: 7] ﴿It almost bursts with rage. Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, "Did no warner come to you?"﴾ [Al-Mulk: 8] ﴿They will say, "Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied him and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything. You are only in great error.'"﴾ [Al-Mulk: 9] ﴿And they will say, "If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze."﴾ [Al-Mulk: 10] ﴿So they will acknowledge their sin, and so, away with the companions of the Blaze!﴾ [Al-Mulk: 11]

(p-5882) ﴿And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾: i.e., the place of return is that burning punishment.

Al-Nasir said: This is from digression (istitrad). When he mentioned the threat against the devils, he digressed to the general threat against the disbelievers.

﴿When they are thrown into it, they will hear from it a roaring﴾ [Al-Mulk: 7]: i.e., to its inhabitants, from among those whose throwing into it preceded them, are the abhorrent sounds, unlike human voices; or to themselves, for they cry out inside it with the voices of abhorrent animals, as in His saying: ﴿For them therein is groaning and roaring﴾ [Hud: 106]. Some said that its very self is meant, by likening its abhorrent, dreadful hissing to the shahiq (roaring), which is the sound that comes out of the chest with force, like the braying of a donkey.

﴿And it boils up﴾ [Al-Mulk: 7]: i.e., it seethes with them and rises up.

﴿It almost bursts with rage﴾ [Al-Mulk: 8]: i.e., its parts almost separate out of rage against those who angered Allah and His Messenger. It is likened, in the intensity of its seething and the strength of its effect on its inhabitants, to a person who is extremely angry at another and exaggerates in inflicting harm upon him; so a form is imagined for it like the form of the established inner state, which is anger that prompts such action. The term "rage" (ghayz) is borrowed for that imagined state, as in the Sharh al-Miftah al-Sharifi. As for the establishment of genuine rage in it, by Allah creating within it perception, that is another discussion. However, it has been said here that there is no need to claim a metaphor in it, because "takad" (almost) rejects it, as in His saying: ﴿Its oil would almost glow﴾ [al-Nur: 35]. The scholars of rhetoric (ma'ani) have stated this in the discussion of hyperbole and exaggeration. It has also been permitted that what is meant is the rage of the angels of punishment (zabaniyah); then the attribution is metaphorical, or there is an elided genitive (mudaf) understood, as in al-Inayah.

﴿Every time a group is thrown into it﴾ [Al-Mulk: 8]: i.e., a company of disbelievers ﴿its keepers will ask them, "Did no warner come to you?"﴾ [Al-Mulk: 8]: i.e., in the world, one who warned you of this punishment.

He said in al-Iklil: From this it is inferred that there is no obligation (taklif) before the sending of a messenger.

(p-5883) ﴿They will say, "Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied him and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything. You are only in great error.'"﴾ [Al-Mulk: 9]: i.e., we denied the messengers and went to excess in denial, to the point that we negated the sending down and the sending at all, and we went far in attributing them to error.

﴿And they will say, "If only we had listened or reasoned"﴾ [Al-Mulk: 10]: i.e., listened to the warnings that came with them, with the listening of one seeking the truth, and reasoned as one who has cast off desire, ﴿we would not be among the companions of the Blaze﴾ [Al-Mulk: 10]: i.e., among the ranks of the people of the Fire.

Two remarks:

The first: Al-Nasir said: Had an astute person reflected on this verse, he would have counted it as evidence for the superiority of hearing over sight, for it has been argued for that from things less clear than it.

The second: Ibn al-Sam'ani said in al-Qawati': It was cited by one who holds that reason is the arbiter (tahkim al-'aql).

Al-Zamakhshari said: It has been said that hearing and reason were combined only because the basis of obligation rests on the proofs of revelation (sam') and reason (aql).

﴿So they will acknowledge their sin, and so, away with the companions of the Blaze!﴾ [Al-Mulk: 11]: i.e., they then acknowledged their denial of the truth and their rejection of the messengers, so far away be they; whether they confess or deny, that will not benefit them.

﴿And keep your speech secret or declare it; indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ That is: of their inner thoughts (ḍamā'ir). So how much more so of what is uttered? The meaning is: fear Him and be mindful of Him.

(p-5884)

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[14] ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.﴾

﴿Should not He who created know?﴾ That is: should He not know the secret and the open of the creation of things? Creation necessitates knowledge, as He said: ﴿And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.﴾ That is: Subtle towards His servants, All-Aware of their deeds. It has also been said that the meaning of the verse is: "Does not Allah know whoever He created, while He is in this position?" In this reading, "man" (man) is the object, and its returning pronoun is implied.

Al-Ghazali said: One deserves the name "al-Latif" (the Subtle) only if he knows the fine and hidden details of affairs and what is delicate among them, and then follows the path of gentleness rather than harshness in bringing about what sets them right. "Al-Khabir" (the All-Aware) is the One whose knowledge does not miss the inner matters, so that not an atom stirs in the dominion and the realm of the unseen, and no soul is still or agitated, except that He has its news. It has the sense of "al-'Alim" (the All-Knowing).

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[15] ﴿It is He who made the earth subservient to you, so walk in its broad tracts and eat of His provision; and to Him is the resurrection.﴾

﴿It is He who made the earth subservient to you﴾, i.e., gentle and easy in its paths.

﴿So walk in its broad tracts﴾, i.e., in its regions and its sides, by way of figurative comparison.

Ibn Jarir said: Because its regions are the counterpart of a person's shoulders (manakib), which are among his extremities.

﴿And eat of His provision﴾, i.e., seek out His bounties, exalted is He.

Al-Shihab said: As for "eating" and "provision," what is intended by them is the seeking of bounties in general and obtaining them, whether by eating or otherwise. It is thus a restriction to the most important and most comprehensive matter, either by way of metaphor or in its literal sense.

He said: If you reflect upon the delights of this world and what is in it, you will find nothing of it belonging to a person except what he eats, and everything else either completes that or repels harm from him. (p-5885)

﴿And to Him is the resurrection﴾, i.e., your rising from your graves for recompense.

Note of caution:

He said in "al-Iklil": In His saying, exalted is He, ﴿So walk in its broad tracts and eat of His provision﴾, there is a command to take means and to earn.

Ibn Kathir said: The verse contains a reminder of His blessing upon His creation in subjecting the earth to them and making it submissive to them, by making it still, not swaying or trembling, owing to what He placed in it of mountains, what He caused springs to gush forth from in it, what He laid out in it of roads, and what He prepared in it of benefits and places for crops and fruits. The meaning is: travel wherever you wish across its regions, and roam about its climes and its expanses in pursuit of all kinds of livelihoods and trades.

﴿And behold, it quakes﴾, meaning: it shakes and trembles violently beneath you, rises above you, and overturns upon you.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[21] ﴿Who is it that can provide for you if He withholds His provision? Nay, they persist in arrogance and aversion.﴾

﴿Who is it that can provide for you if He withholds His provision﴾, meaning the rain and the like. ﴿Nay, they persist﴾, i.e., they go on in their ways, ﴿in arrogance﴾, i.e., obstinacy and transgression, ﴿and aversion﴾, i.e., fleeing from the truth and being proud despite the clarity of its proofs. So they insist on the belief that they are protected from calamities and provided for by the blessing of their gods, and that they are the army that gives victory and the provider, out of stubborn denial and defiance.

The discussion of the Almighty's saying:

[22] ﴿Is one who walks prone on his face better guided, or one who walks upright on a straight path?﴾

﴿Is one who walks prone on his face better guided, or one who walks upright on a straight path?﴾ (p-٥٨٨٨) This is a parable for the astray and the guided. The *mukibb* is the one who stumbles and falls flat on his face because his path is rough and its surface uneven, rising and falling. The one who walks *sawiyy* (upright) is the one who stands firm and is free from stumbling, because his path is level and its surface straight.

Al-Qadi said: The intended meaning is to liken the polytheist and the monotheist to two travellers, and their two religions to two roads. Perhaps the sufficiency of what the word *kabb* (falling on the face) conveys about the state of the road is meant to indicate that what the polytheist follows does not deserve to be called a path. That is why the word "road" (*maslak*) is mentioned for the second and not for the first.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 67, verse 23–26:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[23–26] ﴿Say: "He is the One who brought you into being and made for you hearing, sight, and hearts; little are you grateful."﴾ ﴿Say: "He is the One who scattered you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered."﴾ [al-Mulk: 24] ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ [al-Mulk: 25] ﴿Say: "Knowledge is only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner."﴾ [al-Mulk: 26]

﴿Say: "He is"﴾ meaning: the One who alone deserves worship and that His path be followed, ﴿the One who brought you into being and made for you hearing, sight, and hearts﴾ meaning: the intellects and faculties of perception, ﴿little are you grateful﴾ meaning: by using them for the purpose for which they were created.

﴿Say: "He is the One who scattered you throughout the earth"﴾ [al-Mulk: 24] meaning: He created you upon it so that you would worship Him and uphold the justice He commanded, ﴿and to Him you will be gathered﴾ [al-Mulk: 24] meaning: for recompense.

﴿And they say, "When is this promise"﴾ [al-Mulk: 25] meaning: the Gathering, or the victory of His Messenger and the manifestation of his religion, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ [al-Mulk: 25] meaning: in your warning of it and your instilling of fear through it.

﴿Say: "Knowledge is only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner"﴾ [al-Mulk: 26] meaning: a clarifier of the proof regarding what I warn you of, the collapse of your falsehood when its term comes. As for specifying its time, that is not up to me.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[27] ﴿So when they see it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieved will be distressed, and it will be said: "This is what you used to call for."﴾

﴿So when they see it﴾ i.e., what they were promised of punishment and the vanishing of their falsehood, ﴿approaching﴾ i.e., near, or having nearness, i.e., closeness. ﴿The faces of those who disbelieved will be distressed﴾ i.e., there will appear upon them the signs of being aggrieved: dejection, grief, humiliation and sorrow. ﴿And it will be said﴾ i.e., to them, as a rebuke, ﴿"This is what you used to call for"﴾ i.e., what you used to seek and hasten for through supplication (du'a'), or what you used to claim (tadda'un) — that there is no resurrection — from the claim (da'wa).

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿Say: "Tell me, if God destroys me and those with me, or has mercy on us, who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?"﴾

﴿Say: "Tell me, if God destroys me and those with me, or has mercy on us, who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?"﴾ The disbelievers of Mecca were waiting for the Prophet ﷺ to meet the calamity of fate (rayb al-manun), seeking to be rid of his call and its spread. So he was commanded to say this to them. That is: tell me, if God causes me and those believers with me to die, or has mercy on us by postponing our term and granting us victory, who will protect you from a painful punishment that God has decreed to befall you for your disbelief?

Ibn Kathir said: That is, save yourselves, for there is no one who can rescue you from God except through repentance, turning back to Him, and returning to His religion. The occurrence of what you wish for us of punishment and retribution will not benefit you. Whether God punishes us or has mercy on us, there is no escape for you from His punishment and retribution that has befallen you. The punishment meant is either worldly, namely their humiliation through our victory over them and the repulsion of their misguidance, or otherworldly, which is more severe and more lasting.

(p-5890)

The commentary on His saying, Exalted is He:

[29] ﴿Say, "He is the Most Merciful. We have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied. So you will know who is in clear error."﴾

﴿Say, "He is the Most Merciful. We have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied."﴾ That is: we have depended upon Him in our affairs, not upon what you depend upon of your men and your wealth.

﴿So you will know who is in clear error.﴾ That is: who is in departure from the truth and deviation from its path, from us or from you, when the victory and conquest of Allah come in this world, and his second creation in the Hereafter.

The discussion of the Exalted saying:

[30] ﴿Say: "Have you considered: if your water should become sunken into the earth, who then will bring you flowing water?"﴾

﴿Say: "Have you considered, if your water should become sunken"﴾ meaning: sunk deep, out of reach of buckets; or gone away into the earth. ﴿"who then will bring you flowing water?"﴾ meaning: running, apparent, easily accessible water.

Al-Razi said: The purpose is to remind them of some of the blessings of the Exalted, so as to show them the ugliness of the disbelief they are upon. That is: tell me, if your water becomes gone into the earth, who then will bring you flowing water? They must say: "It is Allah." Then it is said to them at that point: "Why, then, do you make one who has no power over anything at all a partner with Him in worship?" This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you considered the water that you drink?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 68] ﴿Is it you who send it down from the cloud, or are We the sender?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 69] meaning: rather, it is He who sent it down and caused it to flow in springs, out of mercy to the servants; so to Him is all praise.
